title: Stationary consistent equilibrium coalition structures constitute the recursive core
abstract: We study coalitional games where the coalitional payoffs depend on the embedding coalition structure. We introduce a noncooperative, sequential coalition formation model and show that the set of equilibrium outcomes coincides with the recursive core, a generalisation of the core to such games.
summary_en: Kóczy gives a sharp non-cooperative microfoundation for the recursive core. He proves that in coalitional games with externalities, the equilibrium outcomes of a noncooperative sequential coalition-formation game exactly coincide with the recursive core. This 'equivalence theorem' validates the recursive core as the right cooperative-game prediction in environments with externalities: it's not just an abstract solution concept but the natural prediction of strategic non-cooperative play.
data_used: Theoretical model — equivalence proof for partition-function-form games. No primary dataset.
policy_relevance: Theoretical foundation for using the recursive core in applied analyses of EU coalition formation, international climate agreements, and energy-market alliances. The equivalence theorem strengthens the case for recursive-core-based predictions in policy settings.
